page.layout: One printed page, single column of verse with a running head and a decorative headline; page number top left; a catchword-free foot with a signature-like "IN" at lower right (catchword). Faint show-through from the reverse page in the right margin is ignored.

p.i: OVVM potior nuper luctantem Parca peremit.
Spes breuis illa fuit. Ciuis nam pallidus Orci
Cum Furiis totum nunc Acheronta mouet.
GVISIADE extincto cur Gallia tota tumultus
O demum infelix nunc Gallia, terque quaterque!
Hac tibi debuerat morte redire quies.
QVOD Rex Guisiadas violenta morte peremit,
Vt vita, vt regno consuleret, que suo:
Squallida nunc tristes effundit Gallia fletus,
Atque illi passim perfida bella mouet.
Infames lachrymas! infamia bella! quid istis
Fletibus atque armis foedius esse potest?
Guisiadum insidias moeret quod fugerit ille?
Hoc Regi vellet non licuisse suo?

page.notes: The large woodcut initial "O" is read as O. The line "Vt vita, vt regno consuleret, que suo" is doubtful: the word "que" may be "queque" or "quę" [?]. Some verse lines are damaged by the paper; the reading "Ciuis" and "Guisiadē" are doubtful. The catchword "IN" at lower right is printed in roman capitals and is treated as a catchword.
